text:
Predicates:
RankedHighly(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
ActivePlayer(x) ::: x is one of the most active players in major tennis.
LostTo(x, y) ::: x lost to y.
AtRolandGarros2022(x) ::: x participated in Roland Garros 2022.
FemalePlayer(x) ::: x is a female tennis player.
MalePlayer(x) ::: x is a male tennis player.
WTARanked(x) ::: x is ranked highly by the Women's Tennis Association.
LosesToIga(x) ::: x lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRolandGarros2022(x) ::: x participated in Roland Garros 2022.
AtRolandGarros2022(x) ∧ FemalePlayer(x) ::: x is a female player at Roland Garros 2022.
AtRolandGarros2022(x) ∧ MalePlayer(x) ::: x is a male player at Roland Garros 2022.
LostToNadal(x) ::: x lost to Rafael Nadal.
CocoGauff(x) ::: x is Coco Gauff.

Premises:
∀x (RankedHighly(x) → ActivePlayer(x)) ::: If someone is ranked highly by the WTA, then they are among the most active players.
∀x (LosesToIga(x) → RankedHighly(x)) ::: Everyone who lost to Iga Świątek at Roland Garros 2022 is ranked highly by the WTA.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x) ∧ FemalePlayer(x)) → LosesToIga(x) ::: All female players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Iga Świątek.
∀x (AtRolandGarros2022(x)) → (FemalePlayer(x) ∨ MalePlayer(x)) ::: All players at Roland Garros 2022 are either female or male.
∀x (MalePlayer(x) ∧ AtRolandGarros2022(x)) → LostToNadal(x) ::: All male players at Roland Garros 2022 lost to Rafael Nadal.
( (RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∨ LostToNadal(CocoGauff)) ) → ¬MalePlayer(CocoGauff) ::: If Coco Gauff is ranked highly or lost to Nadal, then she is not a male player.
CocoGauff ∈ RolandGarros2022 ::: Coco Gauff participated in Roland Garros 2022.

Conclusion:
( RankedHighly(CocoGauff) ∧ AtRolandGarros2022(CocoGauff) ) → ActivePlayer(CocoGauff) ::: If Coco Gauff is among the highest-ranked players and participated in Roland Garros 2022, then she is among the most active players.
